#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./hsim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  csr) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./hsim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure; QEMU 2 cannot resume from an incomplete
# drain.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

# QEMU 2 leg: orchestrator owns the spawn now that vsim has no
# --qemu-binary path. PYTHONPATH wires the vendored package without
# requiring `pip install -e tools/`.
echo "[$FIXTURE 3/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 2: resume via orchestrator"
ORCH_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG" "$ORCH_LOG"' EXIT
set +e
PYTHONPATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/../tools" timeout "$TIMEOUT" \
  python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume \
    --state "$STATE_VSIM" \
    --mmap "$SHARED_MEM" \
    --size "$SHARED_SIZE" >"$ORCH_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" != "$EXPECT_RC" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: expected exit $EXPECT_RC, got $RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  echo "--- orchestrator log ---"
  cat "$ORCH_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] round-trip exit code $RC"

  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  echo "--- orchestrator log ---"
  cat "$ORCH_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] round-trip exit code $RC"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./hsim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  csr) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./hsim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

# QEMU 2 leg: orchestrator owns the spawn now that vsim has no
# --qemu-binary path. PYTHONPATH wires the vendored package without
# requiring `pip install -e tools/`.
echo "[$FIXTURE 3/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 2: resume via orchestrator"
ORCH_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG" "$ORCH_LOG"' EXIT
set +e
PYTHONPATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/../tools" timeout "$TIMEOUT" \
  python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume \
    --state "$STATE_VSIM" \
    --mmap "$SHARED_MEM" \
    --size "$SHARED_SIZE" >"$ORCH_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" != "$EXPECT_RC" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: expected exit $EXPECT_RC, got $RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  echo "--- orchestrator log ---"
  cat "$ORCH_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] round-trip exit code $RC"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 3 processes (qemu1, vsim, qemu2);
#                the headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's
#                own scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./hsim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip EXPECT_RC=3"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  csr|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of csr|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in csr pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*csr.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
csr_p=${MODE_PASS[csr]} csr_f=${MODE_FAIL[csr]} csr_s=${MODE_SKIP[csr]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((csr_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((csr_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((csr_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: csr ${csr_p}p/${csr_f}f/${csr_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./hsim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip EXPECT_RC=3"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  csr|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of csr|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in csr pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*csr.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
csr_p=${MODE_PASS[csr]} csr_f=${MODE_FAIL[csr]} csr_s=${MODE_SKIP[csr]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((csr_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((csr_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((csr_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: csr ${csr_p}p/${csr_f}f/${csr_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

# ROADMAP - remove the vsim -> QEMU2 leg (everywhere)

> Task: retire the QEMU2 handback / resume leg across the whole repo - code,
> tests, and docs (live + archive + historical). The hybrid flow becomes
> strictly **2-phase**: QEMU1 drain -> vsim resume + drain. The cycle figure is
> the vsim `mcycle` delta (already what `andes-sim` F6 produces). QEMU2's
> round-trip correctness check is intentionally dropped (user decision
> 2026-06-09). One feature at a time; update **State** as you go.

## After-state (the architecture)

```
QEMU1 (drain on trigger, exit 200) --state file + shared mmap--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain, exit 200)
                                                                  ^ cycle figure = vsim mcycle - qemu1 mcycle
```

No third leg. No gdbstub restore. `replay` resumes into vsim only.

## Keep untouched (already correct)

- `driver/*` (plan.hpp, run_plan.*, argv.*, plan_test/itest, ROADMAP.md body) -
  the andes-sim executor already excludes QEMU2.
- `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f6.sh`.

"""Orchestrator CLI entry point.

Subcommands:
  dry-run <plan.yaml>          Parse the plan and print one line per planned
                               spawn. No process is launched.
  run <plan.yaml>              F4/F8: execute every step in the plan; the
                               final spawn's exit code is the CLI return.
  replay-checkpoint <snap>     F10: hydrate a snap/N archive and resume the
                               chosen model from it.
  qemu-resume                  F4-cleanup: spawn QEMU2 from an existing vsim-
                               drained state file + shared mmap. Used by the
                               bash e2e harness now that vsim no longer
                               spawns QEMU itself.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from orchestrator.checkpoint import replay_checkpoint
from orchestrator.plan import Session, load_plan
from orchestrator.runner import (
    cycle_breakdown,
    resume_qemu_from_state,
    run_session,
)


def _format_step_line(idx: int, step) -> str:
    line = f"  step {idx}: model={step.model} trigger={step.trigger.kind}"
    if step.trigger.params:
        params = " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in step.trigger.params.items())
        line += f" ({params})"
    if step.archive_as:
        line += f" archive_as={step.archive_as}"
    return line


def _print_dry_run(session: Session) -> None:
    print(f"session: elf={session.elf} mem_size={session.mem_size}")
    for idx, step in enumerate(session.steps):
        print(_format_step_line(idx, step))


def _print_warmup_breakdowns(state_paths) -> None:
    """F20: render the warmup/measure/total split for every drained state.

    Each line is prefixed with the step index. Steps whose state file has
    no snapshot (qemu drains, or vsim drains with K=0) print
    "warmup: disabled (...)" so the user can still see total cycles
    without conditional log scraping.
    """
    for idx, path in enumerate(state_paths):
        bd = cycle_breakdown(path)
        for line in bd.format_lines():
            print(f"  step {idx}: {line}")


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="orchestrator")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    dry = sub.add_parser(
        "dry-run", help="parse a plan YAML and print planned spawns"
    )
    dry.add_argument("plan", type=Path, help="path to a plan YAML")

    run = sub.add_parser(
        "run", help="execute every step in the plan (F8 N-way loop)"
    )
    run.add_argument("plan", type=Path, help="path to a plan YAML")
    run.add_argument(
        "--project-root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd(),
        help="repo root (default: cwd) used to resolve ELF + artifact paths",
    )
    run.add_argument(
        "--workdir", type=Path, default=None,
        help="persist per-step state files here (default: temp dir, deleted)",
    )
    run.add_argument(
        "--archive-root", type=Path, default=None,
        help=(
            "resolve step.archive_as under this directory "
            "(default: project root)"
        ),
    )

    replay = sub.add_parser(
        "replay-checkpoint",
        help="hydrate a snap/N archive and resume the chosen model",
    )
    replay.add_argument(
        "snap_dir", type=Path,
        help="path to a snap/N directory written by an earlier archive_as",
    )
    replay.add_argument(
        "--resume-with", choices=("vsim", "qemu"), default="vsim",
        help="model to resume the archive with (default: vsim)",
    )
    replay.add_argument(
        "--project-root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd(),
        help="repo root (default: cwd) used to resolve the archived ELF",
    )
    replay.add_argument(
        "--workdir", type=Path, default=None,
        help="persist replay state files here (default: temp dir, deleted)",
    )

    qresume = sub.add_parser(
        "qemu-resume",
        help="spawn QEMU2 from an existing drained state + shared mmap",
    )
    qresume.add_argument(
        "--state", type=Path, required=True,
        help="path to the vsim-drained hybrid_state_v1 binary",
    )
    qresume.add_argument(
        "--mmap", type=Path, required=True,
        help="path to the shared /dev/shm-backed mmap holding workload memory",
    )
    qresume.add_argument(
        "--size", type=int, required=True,
        help="size in bytes of the shared mmap (must match QEMU 1's launch)",
    )
    qresume.add_argument(
        "--project-root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd(),
        help="repo root used to resolve VSIM_QEMU default (default: cwd)",
    )
    qresume.add_argument(
        "--timeout", type=float, default=90.0,
        help="seconds to wait for QEMU2 to exit (default: 90)",
    )

    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "dry-run":
        _print_dry_run(load_plan(args.plan))
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "run":
        session = load_plan(args.plan)
        result = run_session(session, args.project_root,
                             work_dir=args.workdir,
                             archive_root=args.archive_root)
        _print_warmup_breakdowns(result.state_paths)
        return result.exit_code
    if args.cmd == "qemu-resume":
        return resume_qemu_from_state(
            state_path=args.state,
            mmap_path=args.mmap,
            mmap_size=args.size,
            project_root=args.project_root,
            timeout=args.timeout,
        )
    if args.cmd == "replay-checkpoint":
        if args.workdir is not None:
            args.workdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            result = replay_checkpoint(
                snap_dir=args.snap_dir, model=args.resume_with,
                project_root=args.project_root, work_dir=args.workdir,
            )
        else:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="orch-replay-") as tmp:
                result = replay_checkpoint(
                    snap_dir=args.snap_dir, model=args.resume_with,
                    project_root=args.project_root, work_dir=Path(tmp),
                )
        return result.exit_code
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""F8 RED: orchestrator runs an N-step plan and validates each drain state.

The F4 runner hard-codes 3 spawns and rejects any other step count. F8 turns
the runner into a generic loop over `session.steps`, persists each drain's
state file under a caller-provided `work_dir`, and returns a `SessionResult`
exposing the per-step state paths.

This test drives a 2-step drain plan (QEMU drains on CSR enter, vsim drains
on CSR exit) - the minimum N-way shape that exercises step iteration without
also exercising QEMU 2 resume. Both intermediate state files must validate.

Skips with code 77 when any artifact is missing.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import textwrap
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _artifact(name: str, env_key: str, default: Path) -> Path:
    p = Path(os.environ.get(env_key, str(default)))
    if not p.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"{name} not built at {p}")
    return p


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def artifacts() -> dict[str, Path]:
    return {
        "vsim_bin": _artifact(
            "VSIM_BIN", "VSIM_BIN",
            _PROJECT_ROOT / "hybrid_vsim" / "build" / "sim_ax45mpv_premium",
        ),
        "vsim_qemu": _artifact(
            "VSIM_QEMU", "VSIM_QEMU",
            _PROJECT_ROOT / "build" / "qemu" / "qemu-system-riscv64",
        ),
        "vsim_plugin": _artifact(
            "VSIM_PLUGIN", "VSIM_PLUGIN",
            _PROJECT_ROOT / "qemu_plugin" / "libhybrid_handoff.so",
        ),
        "elf": _artifact(
            "VSIM_ELF", "VSIM_ELF",
            _PROJECT_ROOT / "hybrid_vsim" / "hybrid" / "test"
            / "rt_c_v_regs.elf",
        ),
    }


_TWO_STEP_YAML = textwrap.dedent("""\
    session:
      mem_size: 134217728
      mmap_path: null
      elf: hybrid_vsim/hybrid/test/rt_c_v_regs.elf
    steps:
      - model: qemu
        trigger: { kind: csr }
      - model: vsim
        trigger: { kind: csr }
""")


def test_two_step_drain_session_validates_intermediates(
    artifacts: dict[str, Path], tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    from orchestrator.abi import validate_state_file
    from orchestrator.plan import load_plan
    from orchestrator.runner import run_session

    # Plumb env so runner.Artifacts.from_env() picks up the right binaries.
    for key, path in (
        ("VSIM_BIN", artifacts["vsim_bin"]),
        ("VSIM_QEMU", artifacts["vsim_qemu"]),
        ("VSIM_PLUGIN", artifacts["vsim_plugin"]),
    ):
        os.environ[key] = str(path)

    plan_path = tmp_path / "two_step.yaml"
    plan_path.write_text(_TWO_STEP_YAML)
    session = load_plan(plan_path)
    assert len(session.steps) == 2  # sanity

    work_dir = tmp_path / "work"
    work_dir.mkdir()

    result = run_session(session, _PROJECT_ROOT, work_dir=work_dir)

    assert result.exit_code == 0, (
        f"non-zero rc from N-step run: {result.exit_code}"
    )

    # Both spawns drain -> two state files, each must pass ABI validation.
    assert len(result.state_paths) == 2, (
        f"expected 2 state paths, got {result.state_paths}"
    )
    for p in result.state_paths:
        assert p.exists(), f"missing state file: {p}"
        validate_state_file(p)

def replay_checkpoint(
    snap_dir: Path,
    *,
    model: str,
    project_root: Path,
    work_dir: Path,
    artifacts=None,
    spawn_timeout: float = 90.0,
):
    """Hydrate a snap_dir/ archive and resume the chosen model.

    Validates `meta.json` via `validate_replay_meta`, allocates a fresh
    /dev/shm mmap sized to `meta.mem_size`, overwrites it with
    `snap_dir/mem`, copies `snap_dir/state.bin` into `work_dir` as the
    spawn's `state_in`, then drives a synthetic 1-step `Session` through
    `runner.run_session()` with `initial_state_in` pointing at the copy.

    `model='vsim'` -> 1-step `(vsim, csr)` plan; vsim resumes from
                      state_in, executes the ROI, drains on its CSR-exit
                      trigger, exits 200.

    `model='qemu'` -> 1-step `(qemu, end_of_program)` plan; QEMU 2 starts
                      halted under gdbstub, the orchestrator restores
                      state, then continues to workload completion (rc=0).

    Returns the `SessionResult` from `run_session()` unchanged. For vsim,
    `state_paths` has exactly one entry (the drained state); for qemu,
    `state_paths` is empty (`end_of_program` does not produce a state
    file).
    """
    from orchestrator.mmap_owner import MmapOwner
    from orchestrator.plan import Session, Step, TriggerSpec
    from orchestrator.runner import Artifacts, run_session

    meta = json.loads((snap_dir / "meta.json").read_text())
    artifacts = artifacts or Artifacts.from_env(project_root)
    live_cpu_variant = _cpu_variant_from_vsim_path(artifacts.vsim)
    validate_replay_meta(meta, live_cpu_variant=live_cpu_variant)

    mem_size = int(meta["mem_size"])
    elf_path = str(meta["elf_path"])

    work_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    state_in = work_dir / "replay-state-in.bin"
    shutil.copy(snap_dir / "state.bin", state_in)

    trigger_kind = "csr" if model == "vsim" else "end_of_program"
    if model not in {"vsim", "qemu"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported replay model: {model!r}")

    with MmapOwner.allocate(mem_size) as shm:
        shutil.copy(snap_dir / "mem", shm.path)
        synth = Session(
            elf=elf_path,
            mem_size=mem_size,
            mmap_path=str(shm.path),
            steps=(Step(
                model=model,
                trigger=TriggerSpec(kind=trigger_kind, params={}),
            ),),
        )
        return run_session(
            synth, project_root,
            artifacts=artifacts, spawn_timeout=spawn_timeout,
            work_dir=work_dir,
            initial_state_in=state_in,
        )

def cmd_replay(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    snap = Path(args.snap)
    if not snap.is_dir():
        print(f"hsim: snapshot directory not found: {args.snap}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./hsim build",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    argv = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "orchestrator.main", "replay-checkpoint",
        str(snap),
        "--resume-with", args.resume_with,
        "--project-root", str(REPO_ROOT),
    ]
    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"exec: {shlex.join(argv)}")
        return 0

    env = os.environ.copy()
    existing_pp = env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
    tools_dir = str(REPO_ROOT / "tools")
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
        tools_dir + os.pathsep + existing_pp if existing_pp else tools_dir
    )

"""Subprocess factories for QEMU and vsim.

argv builders are pure (no I/O), so they unit-test cleanly. The actual
process spawn goes through `subprocess.Popen` directly in `runner.py`.

The flow is 2-phase: QEMU 1 drains on the plugin trigger, vsim resumes and
drains. There is no QEMU 2 leg -- the vsim -> QEMU2 handback was removed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path


def qemu_drain_argv(qemu_bin: Path, elf: Path, plugin: Path,
                    mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
                    state_out: Path) -> list[str]:
    """QEMU 1: load ELF, drain on plugin's CSR/PC trigger, exit 200."""
    mem_obj = (
        f"memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,"
        f"mem-path={mmap_path},size={mmap_size}"
    )
    return [
        str(qemu_bin),
        "-object", mem_obj,
        "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem",
        "-cpu", "andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512",
        "-nographic",
        "-semihosting-config", "enable=on,target=native",
        "-bios", str(elf),
        "-plugin", f"{plugin},outfile={state_out}",
    ]


def vsim_argv(vsim_bin: Path, elf: Path,
              state_in: Path, state_out: Path,
              mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
              shared_mem_base: int = 0x00000000) -> list[str]:
    """vsim: resume from QEMU 1 state, run ROI, drain, exit 200.

    vsim drains and exits; the cycle figure is its mcycle delta. There is
    no in-process QEMU spawn (the handback was removed).
    """
    return [
        str(vsim_bin),
        str(elf),
        "--resume-from-qemu", str(state_in),
        "--handoff-out", str(state_out),
        "--shared-mem-path", str(mmap_path),
        "--shared-mem-size", str(mmap_size),
        "--shared-mem-base", hex(shared_mem_base),
    ]

"""Subprocess factories for QEMU and vsim.

argv builders are pure (no I/O), so they unit-test cleanly. The actual
process spawn goes through `subprocess.Popen` directly in `runner.py`.

QEMU 2's launch (`qemu_resume_argv`) mirrors `qemu_handback.hpp::spawn_qemu`
in the vsim sources. The key invariant is: in shared-mmap (tier-2) mode,
`-kernel` is OMITTED so QEMU 2 does not re-zero `.bss` / re-load `.data`
on top of phase-2 memory.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import socket
from pathlib import Path


def qemu_drain_argv(qemu_bin: Path, elf: Path, plugin: Path,
                    mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
                    state_out: Path) -> list[str]:
    """QEMU 1: load ELF, drain on plugin's CSR/PC trigger, exit 200."""
    mem_obj = (
        f"memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,"
        f"mem-path={mmap_path},size={mmap_size}"
    )
    return [
        str(qemu_bin),
        "-object", mem_obj,
        "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem",
        "-cpu", "andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512",
        "-nographic",
        "-semihosting-config", "enable=on,target=native",
        "-bios", str(elf),
        "-plugin", f"{plugin},outfile={state_out}",
    ]


def vsim_argv(vsim_bin: Path, elf: Path,
              state_in: Path, state_out: Path,
              mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
              shared_mem_base: int = 0x00000000) -> list[str]:
    """vsim: resume from QEMU 1 state, run ROI, drain, exit 200.

    `--qemu-binary` is intentionally omitted - the orchestrator spawns
    QEMU 2 externally, so vsim's in-process handback path stays dormant
    (see hybrid_vsim/src/main.cpp:478-490, kept for the bash harness).
    """
    return [
        str(vsim_bin),
        str(elf),
        "--resume-from-qemu", str(state_in),
        "--handoff-out", str(state_out),
        "--shared-mem-path", str(mmap_path),
        "--shared-mem-size", str(mmap_size),
        "--shared-mem-base", hex(shared_mem_base),
    ]


def qemu_resume_argv(qemu_bin: Path, mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
                    gdb_port: int) -> list[str]:
    """QEMU 2: start halted under gdbstub. No `-kernel`: shared mmap
    already holds the ELF text/data from QEMU 1's launch."""
    mem_obj = (
        f"memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,"
        f"mem-path={mmap_path},size={mmap_size}"
    )
    return [
        str(qemu_bin),
        "-object", mem_obj,
        "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem",
        "-cpu", "andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512",
        "-bios", "none",
        "-nographic",
        "-semihosting-config", "enable=on,target=native",
        "-gdb", f"tcp::{gdb_port}",
        "-S",
    ]


def pick_free_port() -> int:
    """Ask the kernel for a free loopback port. Subject to a small TOCTOU
    race vs. the QEMU bind that follows; in practice safe enough for
    test-driver use, mirrors `qemu_handback.hpp::pick_free_port`."""
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return s.getsockname()[1]

def _vsim_drain(arts: Artifacts, elf: Path, state_in: Path, state_out: Path,
                shm: MmapOwner, timeout: float) -> None:
    argv = vsim_argv(arts.vsim, elf, state_in, state_out, shm.path, shm.size)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                            stdout=sys.stderr, stderr=sys.stderr)
    rc = _wait(proc, timeout)
    if rc != 200:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"vsim expected exit 200 (drained), got {rc}. argv={argv}"
        )


def resume_qemu_from_state(state_path: Path, mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
                           project_root: Path,
                           timeout: float = 90.0) -> int:
    """One-shot QEMU2 resume from an external vsim-drained state.

    The bash e2e harness owns the mmap and state file; this just spawns
    QEMU2, restores state via gdbstub, and returns QEMU2's exit code.
    Errors (missing files, exec failures) come back as non-zero rc.
    """
    if not state_path.exists():
        print(f"qemu-resume: state file not found: {state_path}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not mmap_path.exists():
        print(f"qemu-resume: mmap path not found: {mmap_path}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    artifacts = Artifacts.from_env(project_root)
    if not artifacts.qemu.exists():
        print(f"qemu-resume: qemu binary not found: {artifacts.qemu}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 127
    with MmapOwner.attach(mmap_path, mmap_size) as shm:
        return _qemu_resume_to_end(artifacts, shm, state_path, timeout)


def _qemu_resume_to_end(arts: Artifacts, shm: MmapOwner, state_in: Path,
                        timeout: float) -> int:
    state = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(state_in.read_bytes())
    port = pick_free_port()
    argv = qemu_resume_argv(arts.qemu, shm.path, shm.size, port)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        restore_and_continue(
            port, state, timeout_sec=10.0,
            child_alive=lambda: proc.poll() is None,
        )
    except ChildDiedDuringConnect:
        return proc.wait(timeout=timeout)
    except Exception:
        proc.kill()
        proc.wait()

                           project_root: Path,
                           timeout: float = 90.0) -> int:
    """One-shot QEMU2 resume from an external vsim-drained state.

    Errors (missing files, exec failures) come back as non-zero rc.

              file=sys.stderr)

    if not mmap_path.exists():

              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    artifacts = Artifacts.from_env(project_root)
    if not artifacts.qemu.exists():
        print(f"qemu-resume: qemu binary not found: {artifacts.qemu}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 127
    with MmapOwner.attach(mmap_path, mmap_size) as shm:
        return _qemu_resume_to_end(artifacts, shm, state_path, timeout)


def _qemu_resume_to_end(arts: Artifacts, shm: MmapOwner, state_in: Path,
                        timeout: float) -> int:
    state = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(state_in.read_bytes())
    port = pick_free_port()
    argv = qemu_resume_argv(arts.qemu, shm.path, shm.size, port)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        restore_and_continue(
            port, state, timeout_sec=10.0,
            child_alive=lambda: proc.poll() is None,
        )
    except ChildDiedDuringConnect:
        return proc.wait(timeout=timeout)
    except Exception:
        proc.kill()
        proc.wait()
        raise
    return _wait(proc, timeout)

"""Checkpoint archive: portable snapshot of a drained spawn.

A snapshot directory holds three artefacts:

  state.bin   raw hybrid_state_v1 (byte copy of the in-flight state file)
  mem         /dev/shm mmap contents at drain time
  meta.json   human-readable descriptor (schema 1; see _build_meta below)

`mem` is large (128 MB by default), so the copy goes through
`cp --reflink=auto` when available - on btrfs/xfs this is a near-instant
COW share; on ext4 the tool transparently falls back to a sequential
copy. If `cp` is missing entirely (unlikely on Linux), Python's
`shutil.copy` takes over.

F10 (checkpoint replay) hydrates a fresh /dev/shm mmap from `mem` and
spawns the chosen model with `--state-in=state.bin`. Validation rules
F10 enforces are encoded in `meta.json` (cpu_variant, vlen_bytes,
mem_size).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from orchestrator.abi import (
    HYBRID_FLAG_FP,
    HYBRID_FLAG_RV64,
    HYBRID_FLAG_V,
    HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC,
    HYBRID_STATE_VERSION,
    HybridStateV1,
)

_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

# QEMU + vsim are both built with VLEN=512 bits today (spawn.py hardcodes
# `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`, and the vsim CMake config picks the same
# CPU variant). 512 bits = 64 bytes. When a future build flips VLEN, this
# constant must move in lock-step with spawn.py - F10's replay validator
# uses it to reject archives captured under a different VLEN.
LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64


def validate_replay_meta(
    meta: dict,
    *,
    live_cpu_variant: str | None,
    live_vlen_bytes: int = LIVE_VLEN_BYTES,
) -> None:
    """Reject archive metadata that would be unsafe to replay.

    Checks (in order, first failure wins):
      - schema == 1
      - abi_version == HYBRID_STATE_VERSION (today: 1)
      - abi_magic (hex string) == HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC
      - cpu_variant matches live binary, when BOTH sides set it; if the
        archive omits cpu_variant, no check (older snapshots stay valid).
      - vlen_bytes matches live VLEN, when archive sets it.

    Field semantics within state.bin (GPR contents, flag bit consistency)
    are not this function's concern - that is enforced by
    `abi.validate_state_file` on the resumed drain.
    """
    schema = meta.get("schema")
    if schema != _SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.schema {schema!r} != expected {_SCHEMA_VERSION}"
        )
    abi_version = meta.get("abi_version")
    if abi_version != HYBRID_STATE_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.abi_version {abi_version!r} != expected "
            f"{HYBRID_STATE_VERSION}"
        )
    abi_magic_raw = meta.get("abi_magic")
    try:
        abi_magic_int = int(abi_magic_raw, 16)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.abi_magic {abi_magic_raw!r} is not a hex string"
        )
    if abi_magic_int != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.abi_magic 0x{abi_magic_int:08x} != expected "
            f"0x{HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:08x}"
        )
    archive_cpu = meta.get("cpu_variant")
    if (archive_cpu is not None and live_cpu_variant is not None
            and archive_cpu != live_cpu_variant):
        raise ValueError(
            f"cpu_variant mismatch: archive={archive_cpu!r} "
            f"live={live_cpu_variant!r}"
        )
    archive_vlen = meta.get("vlen_bytes")
    if archive_vlen is not None and archive_vlen != live_vlen_bytes:
        raise ValueError(
            f"vlen_bytes mismatch: archive={archive_vlen} "
            f"live={live_vlen_bytes}"
        )


def write_archive(
    snap_dir: Path,
    *,
    state_path: Path,
    mmap_path: Path,
    mmap_size: int,
    elf_path: str,
    source_step_index: int,
    cpu_variant: str | None = None,
    region_id: str | None = None,
    slice_index: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Serialise (state.bin, mem, meta.json) into `snap_dir`.

    Creates intermediate directories. Overwrites pre-existing artefacts
    inside `snap_dir` if any. Reads the state struct's `flags` and
    `vlenb` fields to populate meta.json.
    """
    snap_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(state_path, snap_dir / "state.bin")
    _reflink_or_copy(mmap_path, snap_dir / "mem")
    meta = _build_meta(
        state_path=state_path, mmap_size=mmap_size, elf_path=elf_path,
        source_step_index=source_step_index, cpu_variant=cpu_variant,
        region_id=region_id, slice_index=slice_index,
    )
    (snap_dir / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2))


def _build_meta(
    *,
    state_path: Path,
    mmap_size: int,
    elf_path: str,
    source_step_index: int,
    cpu_variant: str | None,
    region_id: str | None,
    slice_index: int | None,
) -> dict:
    state = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(state_path.read_bytes())
    flag_names = []
    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_RV64:
        flag_names.append("RV64")
    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_FP:
        flag_names.append("FP")
    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_V:
        flag_names.append("V")
    meta: dict = {
        "schema": _SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "abi_version": HYBRID_STATE_VERSION,
        "abi_magic": f"0x{HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:08x}",
        "flags": flag_names,
        "vlen_bytes": int(state.vlenb),
        "mem_size": mmap_size,
        "elf_path": elf_path,
        "source_step_index": source_step_index,
        "captured_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    }
    if cpu_variant is not None:
        meta["cpu_variant"] = cpu_variant
    if region_id is not None:
        meta["region_id"] = region_id
    if slice_index is not None:
        meta["slice_index"] = slice_index
    return meta


def _reflink_or_copy(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    """Copy `src` to `dst` using COW when the filesystem supports it.

    btrfs/xfs honour `--reflink=always`; everything else (ext4, tmpfs)
    falls back to a sequential copy via `--reflink=auto`. If `cp` is
    unavailable, use `shutil.copy` as a last resort.
    """
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            ["cp", "--reflink=auto", str(src), str(dst)],
            check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        return
    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        pass
    shutil.copy(src, dst)


def replay_checkpoint(
    snap_dir: Path,
    *,
    model: str,
    project_root: Path,
    work_dir: Path,
    artifacts=None,
    spawn_timeout: float = 90.0,
):
    """Hydrate a snap_dir/ archive and resume the chosen model.

    Validates `meta.json` via `validate_replay_meta`, allocates a fresh
    /dev/shm mmap sized to `meta.mem_size`, overwrites it with
    `snap_dir/mem`, copies `snap_dir/state.bin` into `work_dir` as the
    spawn's `state_in`, then drives a synthetic 1-step `Session` through
    `runner.run_session()` with `initial_state_in` pointing at the copy.

    `model='vsim'` -> 1-step `(vsim, csr)` plan; vsim resumes from
                      state_in, executes the ROI, drains on its CSR-exit
                      trigger, exits 200.

    `model='qemu'` -> 1-step `(qemu, end_of_program)` plan; QEMU 2 starts
                      halted under gdbstub, the orchestrator restores
                      state, then continues to workload completion (rc=0).

    Returns the `SessionResult` from `run_session()` unchanged. For vsim,
    `state_paths` has exactly one entry (the drained state); for qemu,
    `state_paths` is empty (`end_of_program` does not produce a state
    file).
    """
    from orchestrator.mmap_owner import MmapOwner
    from orchestrator.plan import Session, Step, TriggerSpec
    from orchestrator.runner import Artifacts, run_session

    meta = json.loads((snap_dir / "meta.json").read_text())
    artifacts = artifacts or Artifacts.from_env(project_root)
    live_cpu_variant = _cpu_variant_from_vsim_path(artifacts.vsim)
    validate_replay_meta(meta, live_cpu_variant=live_cpu_variant)

    mem_size = int(meta["mem_size"])
    elf_path = str(meta["elf_path"])

    work_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    state_in = work_dir / "replay-state-in.bin"
    shutil.copy(snap_dir / "state.bin", state_in)

    trigger_kind = "csr" if model == "vsim" else "end_of_program"
    if model not in {"vsim", "qemu"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported replay model: {model!r}")

    with MmapOwner.allocate(mem_size) as shm:

"""Checkpoint archive: portable snapshot of a drained spawn.

A snapshot directory holds three artefacts:

  state.bin   raw hybrid_state_v1 (byte copy of the in-flight state file)
  mem         /dev/shm mmap contents at drain time
  meta.json   human-readable descriptor (schema 1; see _build_meta below)

`mem` is large (128 MB by default), so the copy goes through
`cp --reflink=auto` when available - on btrfs/xfs this is a near-instant
COW share; on ext4 the tool transparently falls back to a sequential
copy. If `cp` is missing entirely (unlikely on Linux), Python's
`shutil.copy` takes over.

F10 (checkpoint replay) hydrates a fresh /dev/shm mmap from `mem` and
spawns the chosen model with `--state-in=state.bin`. Validation rules
F10 enforces are encoded in `meta.json` (cpu_variant, vlen_bytes,
mem_size).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from orchestrator.abi import (
    HYBRID_FLAG_FP,
    HYBRID_FLAG_RV64,
    HYBRID_FLAG_V,
    HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC,
    HYBRID_STATE_VERSION,
    HybridStateV1,
)

_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

# QEMU + vsim are both built with VLEN=512 bits today (spawn.py hardcodes
# `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`, and the vsim CMake config picks the same
# CPU variant). 512 bits = 64 bytes. When a future build flips VLEN, this
# constant must move in lock-step with spawn.py - F10's replay validator
# uses it to reject archives captured under a different VLEN.
LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64


def validate_replay_meta(
    meta: dict,
    *,
    live_cpu_variant: str | None,
    live_vlen_bytes: int = LIVE_VLEN_BYTES,
) -> None:
    """Reject archive metadata that would be unsafe to replay.

    Checks (in order, first failure wins):
      - schema == 1
      - abi_version == HYBRID_STATE_VERSION (today: 1)
      - abi_magic (hex string) == HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC
      - cpu_variant matches live binary, when BOTH sides set it; if the
        archive omits cpu_variant, no check (older snapshots stay valid).
      - vlen_bytes matches live VLEN, when archive sets it.

    Field semantics within state.bin (GPR contents, flag bit consistency)
    are not this function's concern - that is enforced by
    `abi.validate_state_file` on the resumed drain.
    """
    schema = meta.get("schema")
    if schema != _SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.schema {schema!r} != expected {_SCHEMA_VERSION}"
        )
    abi_version = meta.get("abi_version")
    if abi_version != HYBRID_STATE_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.abi_version {abi_version!r} != expected "
            f"{HYBRID_STATE_VERSION}"
        )
    abi_magic_raw = meta.get("abi_magic")
    try:
        abi_magic_int = int(abi_magic_raw, 16)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.abi_magic {abi_magic_raw!r} is not a hex string"
        )
    if abi_magic_int != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError(
            f"meta.abi_magic 0x{abi_magic_int:08x} != expected "
            f"0x{HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:08x}"
        )
    archive_cpu = meta.get("cpu_variant")
    if (archive_cpu is not None and live_cpu_variant is not None
            and archive_cpu != live_cpu_variant):
        raise ValueError(
            f"cpu_variant mismatch: archive={archive_cpu!r} "
            f"live={live_cpu_variant!r}"
        )
    archive_vlen = meta.get("vlen_bytes")
    if archive_vlen is not None and archive_vlen != live_vlen_bytes:
        raise ValueError(
            f"vlen_bytes mismatch: archive={archive_vlen} "
            f"live={live_vlen_bytes}"
        )


def write_archive(
    snap_dir: Path,
    *,
    state_path: Path,
    mmap_path: Path,
    mmap_size: int,
    elf_path: str,
    source_step_index: int,
    cpu_variant: str | None = None,
    region_id: str | None = None,
    slice_index: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Serialise (state.bin, mem, meta.json) into `snap_dir`.

    Creates intermediate directories. Overwrites pre-existing artefacts
    inside `snap_dir` if any. Reads the state struct's `flags` and
    `vlenb` fields to populate meta.json.
    """
    snap_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(state_path, snap_dir / "state.bin")
    _reflink_or_copy(mmap_path, snap_dir / "mem")
    meta = _build_meta(
        state_path=state_path, mmap_size=mmap_size, elf_path=elf_path,
        source_step_index=source_step_index, cpu_variant=cpu_variant,
        region_id=region_id, slice_index=slice_index,
    )
    (snap_dir / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2))


def _build_meta(
    *,
    state_path: Path,
    mmap_size: int,
    elf_path: str,
    source_step_index: int,
    cpu_variant: str | None,
    region_id: str | None,
    slice_index: int | None,
) -> dict:
    state = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(state_path.read_bytes())
    flag_names = []
    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_RV64:
        flag_names.append("RV64")
    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_FP:
        flag_names.append("FP")
    if state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_V:
        flag_names.append("V")
    meta: dict = {
        "schema": _SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "abi_version": HYBRID_STATE_VERSION,
        "abi_magic": f"0x{HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:08x}",
        "flags": flag_names,
        "vlen_bytes": int(state.vlenb),
        "mem_size": mmap_size,
        "elf_path": elf_path,
        "source_step_index": source_step_index,
        "captured_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    }
    if cpu_variant is not None:
        meta["cpu_variant"] = cpu_variant
    if region_id is not None:
        meta["region_id"] = region_id
    if slice_index is not None:
        meta["slice_index"] = slice_index
    return meta


def _reflink_or_copy(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    """Copy `src` to `dst` using COW when the filesystem supports it.

    btrfs/xfs honour `--reflink=always`; everything else (ext4, tmpfs)
    falls back to a sequential copy via `--reflink=auto`. If `cp` is
    unavailable, use `shutil.copy` as a last resort.
    """
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            ["cp", "--reflink=auto", str(src), str(dst)],
            check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        return
    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        pass
    shutil.copy(src, dst)


def replay_checkpoint(
    snap_dir: Path,
    *,
    model: str,
    project_root: Path,
    work_dir: Path,
    artifacts=None,
    spawn_timeout: float = 90.0,
):
    """Hydrate a snap_dir/ archive and resume the chosen model.

    Validates `meta.json` via `validate_replay_meta`, allocates a fresh
    /dev/shm mmap sized to `meta.mem_size`, overwrites it with
    `snap_dir/mem`, copies `snap_dir/state.bin` into `work_dir` as the
    spawn's `state_in`, then drives a synthetic 1-step `Session` through
    `runner.run_session()` with `initial_state_in` pointing at the copy.

    `model='vsim'` -> 1-step `(vsim, csr)` plan; vsim resumes from
                      state_in, executes the ROI, drains on its CSR-exit
                      trigger, exits 200.

    `model='qemu'` -> 1-step `(qemu, end_of_program)` plan; QEMU 2 starts
                      halted under gdbstub, the orchestrator restores
                      state, then continues to workload completion (rc=0).

    Returns the `SessionResult` from `run_session()` unchanged. For vsim,
    `state_paths` has exactly one entry (the drained state); for qemu,
    `state_paths` is empty (`end_of_program` does not produce a state
    file).
    """
    from orchestrator.mmap_owner import MmapOwner
    from orchestrator.plan import Session, Step, TriggerSpec
    from orchestrator.runner import Artifacts, run_session

    meta = json.loads((snap_dir / "meta.json").read_text())
    artifacts = artifacts or Artifacts.from_env(project_root)
    live_cpu_variant = _cpu_variant_from_vsim_path(artifacts.vsim)
    validate_replay_meta(meta, live_cpu_variant=live_cpu_variant)

    mem_size = int(meta["mem_size"])
    elf_path = str(meta["elf_path"])

    work_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    state_in = work_dir / "replay-state-in.bin"
    shutil.copy(snap_dir / "state.bin", state_in)

    if model != "vsim":
        raise ValueError(
            f"unsupported replay model: {model!r} "
            f"(only 'vsim' is supported; the QEMU2 resume path was removed)"
        )
    trigger_kind = "csr"

    with MmapOwner.allocate(mem_size) as shm:
        shutil.copy(snap_dir / "mem", shm.path)
        synth = Session(
            elf=elf_path,
            mem_size=mem_size,
            mmap_path=str(shm.path),
            steps=(Step(
                model=model,
                trigger=TriggerSpec(kind=trigger_kind, params={}),
            ),),
        )
        return run_session(
            synth, project_root,
            artifacts=artifacts, spawn_timeout=spawn_timeout,
            work_dir=work_dir,
            initial_state_in=state_in,
        )

    return None

"""Unit tests pinning the QEMU/vsim argv shape.

These are pure-function checks; the e2e test exercises the actual spawn.
The point of these tests is to flag silent argv drift during refactors
(e.g. a missing `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` would compile and run,
but break vector fixtures with illegal-instruction traps).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from orchestrator.spawn import qemu_drain_argv, qemu_resume_argv, vsim_argv


_QEMU = Path("/usr/local/bin/qemu-system-riscv64")
_VSIM = Path("/repo/hybrid_vsim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium")
_ELF = Path("/repo/test.elf")
_PLUGIN = Path("/repo/plugin.so")
_MMAP = Path("/dev/shm/orch-mmap")
_SIZE = 128 * 1024 * 1024
_STATE_IN = Path("/tmp/state-in.bin")
_STATE_OUT = Path("/tmp/state-out.bin")


def test_qemu_drain_argv_loads_elf_via_bios_and_plugin() -> None:
    argv = qemu_drain_argv(_QEMU, _ELF, _PLUGIN, _MMAP, _SIZE, _STATE_OUT)
    assert argv[0] == str(_QEMU)
    assert "-machine" in argv
    machine = argv[argv.index("-machine") + 1]
    assert machine == "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem"
    assert argv[argv.index("-cpu") + 1] == "andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512"
    # -bios <elf> loads the ELF into the shared mmap on QEMU 1.
    assert argv[argv.index("-bios") + 1] == str(_ELF)
    plugin_arg = argv[argv.index("-plugin") + 1]
    assert plugin_arg == f"{_PLUGIN},outfile={_STATE_OUT}"


def test_qemu_resume_argv_omits_kernel_and_runs_halted_under_gdbstub() -> None:
    argv = qemu_resume_argv(_QEMU, _MMAP, _SIZE, gdb_port=12345)
    # -bios none: ELF text already in shared mmap from QEMU 1. Adding
    # -kernel here would re-zero .bss and clobber phase-2 writes.
    assert "-kernel" not in argv
    assert argv[argv.index("-bios") + 1] == "none"
    assert argv[argv.index("-gdb") + 1] == "tcp::12345"
    assert "-S" in argv  # halt at reset; orchestrator restores then `c`s.


def test_vsim_argv_omits_qemu_binary_so_orchestrator_owns_handback() -> None:
    argv = vsim_argv(_VSIM, _ELF, _STATE_IN, _STATE_OUT, _MMAP, _SIZE)
    # The bash harness passes --qemu-binary to trigger vsim's in-process
    # QEMU 2 spawn. The orchestrator must NOT pass it - it spawns QEMU 2
    # externally and drives the gdbstub itself.
    assert "--qemu-binary" not in argv
    assert argv[argv.index("--resume-from-qemu") + 1] == str(_STATE_IN)
    assert argv[argv.index("--handoff-out") + 1] == str(_STATE_OUT)
    assert argv[argv.index("--shared-mem-path") + 1] == str(_MMAP)
    assert argv[argv.index("--shared-mem-size") + 1] == str(_SIZE)
    assert argv[argv.index("--shared-mem-base") + 1] == "0x0"
